newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURK DEMIRBANK SETS UP BANK IN KYRGYZSTA.
newsitem.headline: TURK DEMIRBANK SETS UP BANK IN KYRGYZSTA.

text.p: Demirbank A.S., a medium-sized Turkish bank, said it had set up a bank in the Central Asian republic of Kyrgyzstan with $3 million capital.
The capital was transferred to Kyrgyzstan by April 22 for the establishment of the new bank named Demir Kyrgyz International Bank, Demirbank said in a statement.

Demirbank, whose shares are also listed on the Munich bourse, owns 75 percent of Demir-Halkbank, its Netherlands-based venture with Turkish state Halkbank and 25 percent of Romlease leasing in Romania.

Demirbank had earlier said 40 percent of Demir Kyrgyz bank's shares would be sold to the International Finance Corporation, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and FOM of the Netherlands and 10 percent to a local investor.
